solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unconscious king once known as fool

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
née introduces a woman's former surname
a jerk is a stupid or contemptible person

explanation.surface: A monarch, formerly nicknamed the fool, lies senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconscious' suggests knocked out, but here it means done without thought, as a reflex.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is automatic and unthinking, made without deliberate awareness.

clue.text: Asian ruler smuggled in by deck hand

indicators.note: something smuggled in is concealed inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A sailor working on deck sneaks an Asian monarch aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan was a ruler or sovereign in Central Asia, as with Genghis Khan of the Mongols.

clue.text: Stretchy lace, it's weird

indicators.note: something weird is odd or out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Remarking that some stretchy lace feels odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic describes a material that can be extended and then springs back to shape.

clue.text: Dismissive description of eg Libya's fair punishment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country that is merely, or only, sandy wastes
second meaning: the penalty someone has rightly earned

explanation.surface: Asking whether Libya is getting the punishment it deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'just' as merely and the second word as sandy wastes; the idiom spells the second word with one S.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting your just deserts means receiving the treatment, usually bad, that your actions merit.

clue.text: Unnerve queen and prime minister briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: R stands for regina, Latin for queen
Clement Attlee was British prime minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: A monarch and her premier being rattled for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to make them nervous or flustered, a synonym of unnerve.

clue.text: Grand, in the manner of festival

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
à la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: Something grand, done in the style of a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public occasion or celebration, a synonym for festival.

clue.text: Nut on car shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nut falls on a car and breaks its windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree.

clue.text: Strong dislike of Verona is crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who hates the Italian city calls it mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a deep-seated antipathy or repugnance towards something.

clue.text: Assemble a church service

parts.note: taken as written
Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect together, a synonym of assemble as a verb.

clue.text: Touch European pond creature

parts.note: a touch or a tad is a small amount
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe reaches out to touch an animal in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning a little bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval frog or toad that lives in ponds before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Unpretentious TV abbey mostly covers dirt

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: Downton Abbey is a British TV period drama
dirt and earth both mean soil

explanation.surface: A humble TV series in which a stately home is mostly covered in mud.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece covering another simply sits above it, so 'covers' places the first piece on top rather than around.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-to-earth describes someone practical and modest, free of pretension or airs.

clue.text: Game with tiny, subtle signals

parts.note: tiddly is informal British for very small
winks are discreet signals made with one eye

explanation.surface: A game played by passing small, secret signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly is a British colloquialism meaning very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a table game in which players flick small discs into a cup.

clue.text: Musician to prohibit supporter?

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
a joist is a beam that supports a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: A musician wants to bar a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist is someone who plays the banjo, so a type of instrumental performer.

clue.text: Confront a head of compliance with price

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its leading letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of compliance
a price is what something costs

explanation.surface: Tackling a company's compliance chief about the cost of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly, close in sense to confronting.

clue.text: His pre-match ritual?

parts.note: surface reading: a sportsman's routine before a game
setter's reading: a match is a marriage, so this is a groom's party before his wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' points to sport, but it means a wedding; 'His' marks the men-only celebration, which Americans call a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do is the British name for a groom's night out with friends shortly before his marriage.

clue.text: Lass with large insect is brave

parts.note: a gal is a girl or lass
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A girl faces down a big bug courageously.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means courageous or chivalrous, so a synonym for brave.

clue.text: She finally joins up to get respect

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, keeping only its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of she

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: meets means joins, as roads or rivers do

explanation.surface: A woman at last signs up and earns respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration, a synonym of respect as a noun.

clue.text: A sailor, a philosopher, and a dog

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: It sounds like the start of a joke: a sailor, a philosopher and a dog walk into a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jack Russell is a small, energetic terrier breed originally bred for fox hunting.

clue.text: Police beginning to explore thicket

parts.note: cops is slang for police

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of explore

explanation.surface: Officers starting to search some undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small dense group of trees or bushes, close in meaning to a thicket.

clue.text: Young bird without tail is fashionable

indicators.note: a word without its tail has lost its final letter

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

explanation.surface: A tailless baby bird is somehow stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, a synonym of fashionable.

clue.text: Monkey and donkey close to bridge creating gridlock

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of bridge

explanation.surface: Animals near a bridge are holding up the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' here is the playful term for a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where no progress is possible, as gridlock is figuratively.

clue.text: Make it to car he wrecked

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arriving at a car that someone has smashed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive there, the same as to make it to it.

clue.text: Draw river? Piece of cake!

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Sketching a river turns out to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake!' reads as the idiom for something easy, but it is literal: one layer of a wedding cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of the stacked layers making up a tall celebration cake.

clue.text: Forceful chimp ate bananas

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A powerful ape devoured some bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means expressed with force and conviction, a synonym of forceful.
